The stock of the Chinese pharmaceutical producer and distributor closed the regular session at $4.27, down 6.77%, according to
The move follows eight Schedule 13G filings submitted to the

on Tuesday. A Schedule 13G is a short-form beneficial ownership report filed when an investor acquires more than 5% of a public company’s equity securities without the intent to change or influence control of the issuer.
The filings disclosed that British Virgin Islands-registered entities, each wholly owned by a single individual, now hold the bulk of Universe Pharmaceuticals’ Class A shares.
, holds the largest stake at 18.30%, roughly twice the size of any other single filer.
Seven other entities hold stakes ranging from 9.29% to 9.98%.
Shareholders To Vote On Reverse Split
In a separate Tuesday filing, Universe Pharmaceuticals also announced its annual general meeting, set for Sept. 30.
Shareholders of record as of Aug. 31 will vote on re-electing five directors and on a proposed 1-for-10 share consolidation.
Shares Trace Back To Patent Acquisition
The disclosed ownership stakes correspond to shares issued as consideration for Universe Pharmaceuticals’ acquisition of

The deal, first outlined in a share purchase agreement dated Jun. 17, gave the company five China-based patents covering pharmaceutical compounds and drug-delivery technologies targeting age-related diseases, neurodegenerative conditions, cognitive disorders and cardiovascular applications

Universe Pharmaceuticals issued 4.37 million Class A ordinary shares as consideration for the deal, restricted securities issued under an exemption from standard registration requirements. Following the issuance, the company now has 5.01 million Class A ordinary shares and 16,077 Class B ordinary shares outstanding.
Universe Pharmaceuticals has a market capitalization of $21.45 million, a 52-week high of $17.96 and a 52-week low of $2.
The Relative Strength Index (RSI) of UPC stands at 41.78.
The stock has risen 21.65% over the past 12 months.
UPC is currently positioned near the lower end of its 52-week range, at about 14.2% of the annual band.
